div.div: This document has been developed by Lika Cranes, to provide a means by which it is possible to record the findings of a crane survey and categorise the findings in terms of criticality in relation to continued crane operational service.

It is the responsibility of the person carrying out the inspection to ensure that all findings are noted. However, where a situation arises that prevents either a thorough inspection or condition evaluation, then the person performing the inspection must make note accordingly.
The format of the survey checklist includes a condition evaluation selection with definitions as follows:

tr.td: Good Operational Condition, continue with regular maintenance and inspection.

Corrective Action identified but operating performance is not compromised, if not addressed in appropriate timescale performance issue may result, CCE corrective action requires to be completed before the next scheduled annual crane condition evaluation.

Unsafe Condition identified, these apply to critical operational systems which mean the crane sub system or in certain instances the crane cannot be safely operated. Therefore the CRANE SYSTEM / CRANE IS NOT TO BE USED until the deficiency is repaired or an alternative solution is found subject to the approval of the authorized personnel.

div.div: The final survey report would normally be distributed via the Lika support engineer.
Prior to leaving the rig the surveyor must leave a copy of each crane summary report with the responsible installation parties such as maintenance supervisor, rig supervisor or OIM.
Condition Evaluation : - an assessment of equipment condition.
Condition Evaluation Checklist: - a compilation of checks, to be made, with criteria applicable to a particular make and model of crane.

Condition Evaluation Report: - a standardised report, describing the findings of the condition evaluation shall consist of the completed checklist, plus a summary of the findings and recommendations. The findings shall be reported as:

tr.td: Good Operational Condition, continue with regular maintenance and inspection as defined within the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS)

Corrective Action identified but operating performance is not compromised, if not addressed in an appropriate timescale performance issue may result, CCE corrective action requires to be completed before the next scheduled annual crane condition evaluation.

Unsafe Condition identified, these apply to critical operational systems which mean the crane sub system or in certain instances the crane cannot be safely operated. Therefore, the CRANE SUB SYSTEM / CRANE IS NOT TO BE USED until the deficiency is repaired or an alternative solution is found subject to the approval of the ICP / SME / RMA.

div.div: Crane condition evaluations are performed to meet quality system requirements for hardware inspections, compliance audits or when taking over management of a rig.
All inspection work will be completed under and comply with the companies SMS (Safety Management System) requirements including the requirements for task planning and risk assessment.
Obtain a Permit to Work, prior to commencing any work on the Cranes
Ensure all guards are in place prior to running any of the crane machinery
Ensure that all fluid systems are relieved of pressure prior to disconnecting any lines of fitting.
Ensure that adequate provision has been made to safely contain and dispose of oil, fuel and coolant, waste.

Before carrying out any maintenance on the hydraulic system, ensure; the crane is shut down and the boom in the rest, the hydraulic oil system isolated, pressure relieved from the system the engine start is inhibited.
DO NOT START warning notices have been clearly displayed
Before carrying out maintenance work on the electrical system ensure that: Electrical Isolation Work Permit has been issued, isolations have been put in place and witnessed by the Lika Engineers.
All electrical equipment has been isolated; fuses removed and suitable warning notices posted.

The purpose of the crane condition evaluation is to assess the condition of the cranes, with a minimum amount of disassembly and with a minimum amount of disruption to operations. It is not intended to replace the routine planned maintenance requirements performed aboard the vessel / rig.

Some crane components cannot be fully inspected without removal from the crane, or without major disassembly, as in the case of , engines, pumps, winches and crane booms. However, the following techniques will be used to ensure a meaningful assessment is performed:-
Review of certification and maintenance records

Magnetic Particle and Ultrasound Inspection of structural components and hooks and fittings are part of the regular planned maintenance programme. MPI/UT will be performed as part of the condition evaluation, if the regularly scheduled MPI/UT is overdue, or in the event visual inspections reveal the need for additional MPI/UT.
